description: Team Avalon is all about helping NASA establish a lunar base on the moon, and to do that we are going to create the interface explaining where we can land on the lunar poles. These areas are where water is stored as ice, and serves as a valuable resource for establishing a lunar base. Through a web design that can be useful to people on both the Earth and Moon alike, this project will use the most recent data from NASA as well as AI integration to give detailed descriptions of the lunar surface.
summary:
LUNARIS is an intelligent lunar landing site assessment platform developed to support safer, more efficient mission planning in the Moon’s south polar region. Using NASA lunar datasets, including LOLA topography, LUNARIS evaluates candidate landing regions by assessing terrain, solar illumination, Sun and Earth visibility, and potential direct-to-Earth communication windows over configurable 24-, 48-, and 72-hour mission timelines.

What sets it apart is its intelligent cross-scenario comparison. Instead of mission planners having to navigate separate tools and interpret isolated datasets, LUNARIS lets them compare multiple landing locations and mission scenarios, identify operational constraints, and evaluate the trade-offs between power availability, communication access, and terrain conditions. This supports more informed site selection and provides a framework for reassessing plans when mission requirements, schedules, or constraints change.

LUNARIS addresses a critical challenge in lunar exploration: the extreme and highly variable lighting and communication conditions at the south pole. By translating complex lunar environmental data into an accessible, comparative planning interface, it aims to help mission planners identify more viable landing regions and support long-term infrastructure decisions, including the selection of future lunar base locations. LUNARIS was built to so lunar sites are selected with the right data to make our dreams of a lunar base a reality.
details:
LUNARIS is a web-based lunar mission-planning platform designed to evaluate and compare potential landing regions in the Moon's south polar environment. Users can configure mission scenarios by selecting geographic coordinates, landing dates, and mission durations. The platform uses lunar topographic data to assess local terrain and environmental conditions, while its mission timeline functionality allows conditions to be examined over 24-, 48-, and 72-hour periods.

LUNARIS focuses on three critical considerations for lunar operations: solar illumination and power availability, Earth visibility and direct-to-Earth communication opportunities, and local terrain conditions that can influence the operational environment. Rather than examining each location independently, LUNARIS holistically takes all these factors into context so users can create alternative scenarios and compare their results to understand how changing a landing location or mission configuration affects feasibility.

The Moon's south pole presents substantial challenges because crater walls, elevated ridges, and complex terrain create significant variations in sunlight and Earth visibility. A landing site may offer favourable conditions in one respect while presenting serious limitations in another. LUNARIS brings these considerations into a unified planning environment, helping users identify constraints and make more informed decisions.

Its intended impact extends beyond individual landings. By supporting comparative analysis over longer mission timelines, LUNARIS could contribute to evaluating candidate regions for future lunar infrastructure, including sustained surface operations and potential lunar base development. It also aims to make complex lunar mission data more accessible to students, educators, and the wider public.

LUNARIS was developed as a full-stack web application using:

  • React and JavaScript: Interactive frontend and mission-planning interface.
  • Vite: Frontend development and build environment.
  • Python and FastAPI: Backend services and scientific data processing.
  • NASA LOLA (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter) elevation data: High-resolution lunar topographic information, using the LDEM 60S 240MPP dataset at approximately 240-metre resolution.
  • Firebase Hosting: Deployment of the public-facing application.
  • Render: Hosting of the backend API.
  • Git and GitHub: Version control and collaborative development workflow.

LUNARIS's central innovation is its cross-scenario assessment approach. Instead of simply displaying maps or individual environmental measurements, it brings multiple candidate locations and mission timelines into one comparative workspace. This helps reveal trade-offs that might otherwise be difficult to identify when using separate scientific tools.

During development, we considered the relationship between terrain, illumination, communication availability, mission duration, and changing operational requirements. We also considered usability: complex scientific information needs to be presented in a way that supports both technical assessment and rapid decision-making.

Ultimately, LUNARIS aims to bridge the gap between raw lunar environmental data and practical mission planning, supporting more adaptable, informed, and cost-conscious decisions as humanity prepares for sustained exploration of the Moon.
